proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), and \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\), and put \(t_e=T_j+h\).  Since \(h\geq 0\), \(t_e\geq T_j\), so \texttt{ass:consistency} gives
\[
Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{j,t_e}=Y_{j,t_e}(1).
\]
If \(w_{jh,i}>0\), then either \(i\in D_{jh}\), under the nested rule, or \(i\in D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\), under the deep rule; the inclusion follows from \(h\leq K\).  Thus \(T_i>t_e\), and the same consistency assumption gives
\[
Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{i,t_e}=Y_{i,t_e}(0).
\]
Using the definition of \(\tau_e\), cancellation of the treated potential outcome yields, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e
&=Y_{j,t_e}(1)-\sum_iw_{jh,i}Y_{i,t_e}(0)
  -\{Y_{j,t_e}(1)-Y_{j,t_e}(0)\}\\
&=Y_{j,t_e}(0)-\sum_iw_{jh,i}Y_{i,t_e}(0)\\
&=a_e(w)^{\top}Q.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last equality uses the definitions of the deduplicated vector \(Q\) and row \(a_e(w)\); deduplication merely makes a reused cell one common coordinate and does not change this linear contrast.  By \texttt{ass:gaussian-law}, conditional on \(x\) and \(T_{\mathrm{adopt}}\),
\[
Q=m+\varepsilon,\qquad \varepsilon\sim N(0,\Sigma_Q).
\]
Stacking the preceding identities in the fixed order of \(\mathcal E\) therefore gives
\[
\widehat\tau(w)-\tau=A(w)m+A(w)\varepsilon
\sim N\!\left(A(w)m,\,A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\right),
\]
which proves both the coordinate identity and the asserted joint Gaussian mean and covariance.

Fix \(e=(j,h)\), put \(t=T_j+h\), and define the predictor discrepancy
\[
d_e(w)=x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i.
\]
By \texttt{ass:mean-structure} and the definition of \(a_e(w)\),
\[
a_e(w)^{\top}m
=d_e(w)^{\top}\beta_t+r_{jt}-\sum_iw_{jh,i}r_{it}.
\]
Cauchy--Schwarz, \texttt{ass:coefficient-radius}, \texttt{ass:cellwise-misspecification}, and the simplex identities \(w_{jh,i}\geq0\) and \(\sum_iw_{jh,i}=1\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left|a_e(w)^{\top}m\right|
&\leq \lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2\lVert\beta_t\rVert_2
   +|r_{jt}|+\sum_iw_{jh,i}|r_{it}|\\
&\leq L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\frac\delta2
   +\frac\delta2\sum_iw_{jh,i}\\
&=L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\delta=b_e(w).
\end{aligned}
\]
It remains to prove that this support-function bound is exact.  If \(d_e(w)\neq0\), set
\[
\beta_t=L\frac{d_e(w)}{\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2};
\]
if \(d_e(w)=0\), set \(\beta_t=0\).  Set \(r_{jt}=\delta/2\) and \(r_{it}=-\delta/2\) for every donor with positive weight.  The focal cell is distinct from every donor cell because \(T_j\leq t<T_i\) for a donor \(i\), so these assignments are consistent.  Set all remaining coefficient and remainder coordinates to zero and define \(m\) by \texttt{ass:mean-structure}.  These choices satisfy the two radius assumptions and give
\[
a_e(w)^{\top}m=L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\delta=b_e(w).
\]
Negating the displayed choices of \(\beta_t\) and \(r\) gives \(a_e(w)^{\top}m=-b_e(w)\).  Each choice extends to a member of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}\): take \(Q\sim N(m,\Sigma_Q)\), choose arbitrary treated potential outcomes, and define observed outcomes by \texttt{ass:consistency}; the fixed covariance already obeys the covariance-band requirement.  Hence both endpoints are attainable and the supremum of the absolute bias is exactly \(b_e(w)\).

For \(e=(j,h)\), call \(c_e=(j,T_j+h)\) its focal cell.  The cells \(c_e\) are distinct as \(e\) varies: equality of two such cells first forces the same unit \(j\), and then the same horizon.  Moreover, no \(c_e\) can be a donor cell in any contrast row.  Indeed, if the same cell were a donor cell in a row observed at calendar time \(t=T_j+h\), donor eligibility would require \(T_j>t\), whereas \(t\geq T_j\), a contradiction.  Thus, after putting the \(M\) focal-cell columns first, the deduplicated contrast matrix has the block form
\[
A(w)=\begin{bmatrix}I_M&B(w)\end{bmatrix}.
\]
Consequently
\[
A(w)A(w)^{\top}=I_M+B(w)B(w)^{\top}\succeq I_M.
\]
The simplexes in both support rules are nonempty: \texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} gives nonemptiness of \(D_{jK}\), and nesting gives \(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\).  For every feasible row, its focal coordinate is disjoint from its donor coordinates and the simplex restrictions give
\[
\lVert a_e(w)\rVert_2^2=1+\sum_iw_{jh,i}^2
\leq1+\left(\sum_iw_{jh,i}\right)^2=2.
\]
Now apply both sides of \texttt{ass:covariance-band}.  Congruence preserves the Loewner order, so
\[
A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}
\succeq\sigma_{\min}A(w)A(w)^{\top}
\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M.
\]
For a coordinate row, the same assumption gives
\[
\sigma_{\min}\lVert a_e(w)\rVert_2^2
\leq a_e(w)^{\top}\Sigma_Qa_e(w)
=\operatorname{sd}_e(w)^2
\leq\sigma_{\max}\lVert a_e(w)\rVert_2^2.
\]
Since the focal coefficient equals one, \(\lVert a_e(w)\rVert_2^2\geq1\); combining this fact with the preceding upper norm bound proves
\[
\sigma_{\min}\leq\operatorname{sd}_e(w)^2\leq2\sigma_{\max}.
\]

Write \(\overline\Phi(x)=1-\Phi(x)\), let \(\varphi(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}\), and abbreviate \(q_m=q_\alpha(m)\) and \(z_m=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/(2m))\).  Independence in the definition of \(q_m\) gives
\[
1-\alpha=\{1-2\overline\Phi(q_m)\}^{m}.
\]
In particular \(q_m>0\), because \(1-\alpha>1/2\).

We first give an elementary lower bound for \(q_m\).  For every \(x\geq1\), monotonicity of \(\varphi\) on \([0,\infty)\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\overline\Phi(x)
&\geq\int_x^{x+1/x}\varphi(u)\,du
\geq\frac1x\varphi(x+1/x)\\
&\geq c_0\frac{e^{-x^2/2}}x,
\qquad c_0=\frac{e^{-3/2}}{\sqrt{2\pi}},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the last step uses \((x+1/x)^2/2\leq x^2/2+3/2\).  If \(m\geq3\) and \(q_m\leq\sqrt{\log m}\), this inequality, together with \(\overline\Phi(q_m)\geq\overline\Phi(1)\geq\varphi(2)\) when \(q_m<1\), yields in both cases
\[
\overline\Phi(q_m)\geq c_0\frac{m^{-1/2}}{\sqrt{\log m}}.
\]
Here the case \(q_m<1\) uses \(m^{-1/2}/\sqrt{\log m}\leq e^{-1/2}\) for \(m\geq3\) and \(c_0e^{-1/2}=\varphi(2)\).  Hence
\[
1-\alpha
\leq\exp\{-2m\overline\Phi(q_m)\}
\leq\exp\!\left\{-2c_0\sqrt{m/\log m}\right\}.
\]
Because the last expression tends to zero, there is an integer \(m_0\geq3\), depending only on \(\alpha\), for which it is strictly smaller than \(1-\alpha\) for every \(m\geq m_0\).  The supposition is then impossible, and therefore
\[
q_m>\sqrt{\log m}\qquad(m\geq m_0).
\]

For the numerator, the exponential Markov inequality applied to a standard normal \(G\) gives, for \(x\geq0\),
\[
\overline\Phi(x)=\Pr(G\geq x)
\leq e^{-x^2}\mathbb E e^{xG}=e^{-x^2/2}.
\]
Since \(z_m>0\) and \(\overline\Phi(z_m)=\alpha/(2m)\), it follows that
\[
z_m\leq\sqrt{2\log(2m/\alpha)}.
\]
For \(m\geq m_0\), the preceding two displays imply
\[
\frac{z_m+1}{q_m}
\leq
\sqrt{2\left(1+\frac{\log(2/\alpha)}{\log m_0}\right)}
+\frac1{\sqrt{\log m_0}}.
\]
For \(1\leq m<m_0\), there are only finitely many positive denominators \(q_m\).  Taking the larger of the displayed constant and those finitely many ratios proves \(c_\alpha<\infty\).  Finally, the outward-rounded calibration condition in the definition of \(z_B\) gives
\[
z_B<z_M+1\leq c_\alpha q_\alpha(M),
\]
and hence the claimed weak inequality.

Fix a support rule \(s\).  For \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), define the deterministic envelope
\[
H_s(w)=\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\{b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}.
\]
By \texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} and nesting, \(\mathcal F_s\) is a nonempty finite product of compact simplexes.  The functions in the maximum are continuous norms of affine functions of \(w\), so \(H_s\) attains its minimum.

The program in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} is exactly an epigraph formulation of this minimum.  Indeed, every feasible \((w,u,v,g)\) satisfies
\[
b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)
\leq Lu_e+\delta+z_Bv_e\leq g
\quad(e\in\mathcal E),
\]
whereas, for any \(w\), choosing \(u_e=\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\rVert_2\), \(v_e=\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\), and \(g=H_s(w)\) is feasible.  Thus
\[
\Gamma_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}H_s(w),
\]
and the weight component of every optimizer has \(H_s(w)=\Gamma_s\).

For coverage, \texttt{lem:prediction-error} and \texttt{lem:bias-radius} give, under every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}\),
\[
\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e=\mu_e+Z_e,
\qquad |\mu_e|\leq b_e(w),
\]
where \(Z=(Z_e)_{e\in\mathcal E}\) is centered Gaussian and \(Z_e/\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\sim N(0,1)\).  Therefore the event
\[
\mathcal G=\bigcap_{e\in\mathcal E}
\{|Z_e|\leq z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}
\]
is contained in the asserted band-coverage event.  No independence is required: the union bound and the certified tail inequality for \(z_B\) give
\[
\Pr_P(\mathcal G^c)
\leq\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}2\{1-\Phi(z_B)\}
=2M\{1-\Phi(z_B)\}\leq\alpha.
\]
This is finite-sample and uniform because the bound uses only the declared bias support function and the fixed covariance.

Finally, all coefficients in the finite record of \texttt{def:finite-input} are rational.  Each predictor-norm constraint is the Lorentz-cone membership
\[
\left(u_{jh},x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right)\in\mathcal L_{p+1},
\]
and each noise-norm constraint is
\[
\left(v_{jh},R_Qa_{jh}(w)\right)\in\mathcal L_{|\mathcal C|+1}.
\]
Simplex restrictions and epigraph inequalities use nonnegative orthants and rational linear equalities after slack variables are introduced; free variables may be split into positive and negative parts.  This is precisely the rational standard-form product-cone record in \texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}.  The transformations preserve feasible objective values in both directions, so its value is \(\Gamma_s\), as claimed.

Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  By \texttt{thm:socp-coverage}, an optimizing SOCP weight and the half-widths
\[
\ell_e=b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)
\]
are feasible in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} and have maximum \(\Gamma_s\).  Hence
\[
W_s\leq\Gamma_s.
\]

For the reverse comparison, take any pair \((w,\ell)\) feasible in the definition of \(W_s\), and put
\[
R=\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e.
\]
First, \(b_e(w)\leq R\) for every \(e\).  Otherwise, \texttt{lem:bias-radius} supplies a law \(P_e\) in the model class under which the coordinate error is Gaussian with mean \(b_e(w)>R\geq\ell_e\).  Under that law,
\[
\Pr_{P_e}\{|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e\}
\leq\Pr_{P_e}\{\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e\leq\ell_e\}<\frac12.
\]
The simultaneous coverage probability is no larger than this marginal probability, contradicting \(1-\alpha>1/2\).  Thus
\[
\max_e b_e(w)\leq R.
\]

Second, we derive a dimension-uniform stochastic lower bound on \(R\).  The model class contains the centered law \(P_0\) obtained by setting \(\beta=0\), \(r=0\), and hence \(m=0\).  Under \(P_0\), \texttt{lem:prediction-error} gives a centered Gaussian error \(Z\) with covariance
\[
V=A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M
\]
by \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry}.  Write \(V=\sigma_{\min}I_M+C\) with \(C\succeq0\), and on an auxiliary product space let
\[
X\sim N(0,\sigma_{\min}I_M),\qquad U\sim N(0,C)
\]
be independent.  Then \(X+U\) has the same law as \(Z\).

We now prove the required Gaussian-cube comparison directly, including singular \(C\).  Put \(s_0=\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}\) and, for \(R>0\),
\[
g_R(u)=\Pr\{|s_0G+u|\leq R\},\qquad G\sim N(0,1).
\]
The function is even.  For \(u\geq0\), differentiation gives
\[
g_R'(u)=\frac1{s_0}\left\{
\varphi\left(\frac{R+u}{s_0}\right)
-\varphi\left(\frac{R-u}{s_0}\right)\right\}\leq0,
\]
because \(|R+u|\geq|R-u|\) and the standard normal density decreases with absolute value.  Hence \(g_R(u)\leq g_R(0)\).  Conditional on \(U=u\), independence of the coordinates of \(X\) therefore gives
\[
\Pr\{X+u\in[-R,R]^M\}
=\prod_{k=1}^Mg_R(u_k)
\leq g_R(0)^M
=\Pr\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}.
\]
Integration with respect to the possibly degenerate Gaussian law of \(U\) proves
\[
\Pr\{Z\in[-R,R]^M\}
\leq\Pr\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}.
\]
The same conclusion is immediate for \(R=0\).

Honesty of \((w,\ell)\) under \(P_0\), inclusion of its rectangle in the cube, and the preceding comparison now imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
1-\alpha
&\leq\Pr_{P_0}\{|Z_e|\leq\ell_e\text{ for every }e\}\\
&\leq\Pr_{P_0}\{Z\in[-R,R]^M\}\\
&\leq\Pr\left\{\max_{1\leq k\leq M}|G_k|\leq
\frac{R}{\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}}\right\},
\end{aligned}
\]
where the \(G_k\) are independent standard normals.  The last probability is strictly increasing in its nonnegative threshold, so the definition of \(q_\alpha(M)\) yields
\[
R\geq\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}\,q_\alpha(M).
\]

By \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry} and \texttt{lem:gaussian-quantile-ratio},
\[
\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\leq\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}}
\quad\text{and}\quad
z_B\leq c_\alpha q_\alpha(M).
\]
Combining all established inequalities gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Gamma_s
&\leq\max_e\{b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}\\
&\leq R+c_\alpha q_\alpha(M)\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}}\\
&\leq\left(1+c_\alpha\sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}}\right)R.
\end{aligned}
\]
This holds for every honest deterministic pair \((w,\ell)\); taking the infimum over such pairs proves
\[
\Gamma_s\leq
\left(1+c_\alpha\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}/\sigma_{\min}}\right)W_s.
\]
The comparison factor contains only \(\alpha\) and the fixed covariance-band ratio, so it is independent of all dimensions, adoption and overlap patterns, predictors, and donor geometry listed in the statement.

Suppose \(M=1\), \(\delta=0\), and the chosen feasible weight satisfies
\[
x_j-\sum_iw_ix_i=0.
\]
Then the definition \(b(w)=L\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_ix_i\rVert_2+\delta\) gives \(b(w)=0\).  The band supplied by \texttt{thm:socp-coverage} is consequently
\[
\widehat\tau(w)\pm z_B\operatorname{sd}(w),
\]
which is the known-covariance Gaussian interval with a certified, possibly conservative, critical value.

Let \(z_\star=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\).  Given any \(\varepsilon>0\), density of the rationals supplies
\[
z_\star<q<z_\star+\min\{\varepsilon,1\},\qquad q\in\mathbb Q.
\]
Strict monotonicity of \(\Phi\) then gives
\[
2\{1-\Phi(q)\}<\alpha,
\qquad
q<\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)+1.
\]
Thus \(q\) satisfies the two calibration inequalities for \(M=1\) and approaches \(z_\star\) from above as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).  These strict inequalities admit finite outward-rounded rational certificates: truncate the Gaussian integral with its elementary exponential tail bound, and enclose the exponential on the remaining compact interval by convergent rational Taylor bounds; refinement makes the rational enclosure smaller than either strict gap.  Therefore the approximating rationals can be supplied as certified multipliers in the sense of the definition of \(z_B\).

Fix \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal E\), \(0\le h\le K\).  If \(i\in D_{jK}\), then the definition of the donor sets gives
\[
T_i>T_j+K\ge T_j+h,
\]
and hence \(i\in D_{jh}\).  Therefore
\[
D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\qquad\text{for every }(j,h)\in\mathcal E.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:donor-feasibility}\) states that every \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty, so all deepest-pool simplexes below are nonempty.  Moreover, if \(v\in\Delta(D_{jK})\), then \(v_i\ge0\), \(v_i=0\) for \(i\notin D_{jK}\), and \(\sum_{i\in D_{jK}}v_i=1\).  The displayed set inclusion implies that \(v_i=0\) also for every \(i\notin D_{jh}\), while
\[
\sum_{i\in D_{jh}}v_i
=\sum_{i\in D_{jK}}v_i+
  \sum_{i\in D_{jh}\setminus D_{jK}}v_i
=1.
\]
Thus \(\Delta(D_{jK})\subseteq\Delta(D_{jh})\) for each coordinate.  Taking the product over \(\mathcal E\), as prescribed by the definition of \(\mathcal F_s\), yields
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}.
\]

For the exact-width comparison, let \(\mathcal H_s\) be the set of pairs \((w,\ell)\) satisfying all constraints in \(\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}\) under support rule \(s\).  Concretely, membership requires \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), \(\ell\in[0,\infty)^M\), determinism of \(w\) and \(\ell\) conditional on the fixed inputs, and
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}
P\!\left\{
\left|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e\right|\le\ell_e
\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E
\right\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The last three requirements and the objective \(\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e\) do not depend on \(s\).  Hence the feasible-set inclusion just proved gives
\[
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal H_{\mathrm{nested}}.
\]
Monotonicity of an infimum under enlargement of its feasible set, applied directly to \(\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}\), now gives
\[
W_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{nested}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
\le
\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{deep}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
=W_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\]
This argument remains valid if an honesty-feasible set is empty, using the extended-value convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\) already allowed by the codomain of \(W_s\).

For the SOCP comparison, let \(\mathcal S_s\) denote the feasible set of quadruples \((w,u,v,g)\) in \(\texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}\).  Every constraint other than \(w\in\mathcal F_s\) is the same for the two support rules: for every \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\),
\[
\left\|x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right\|_2\le u_{jh},
\qquad
\left\|R_Qa_{jh}(w)\right\|_2\le v_{jh},
\qquad
Lu_{jh}+\delta+z_Bv_{jh}\le g.
\]
Consequently, \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}\) implies
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}.
\]
The objective is the same scalar \(g\) on both sets.  Therefore, by the minimization in \(\texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}\),
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}}g
\le
\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}}g
=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\]
Together, the two inequalities prove the proposition for every admissible fixed design.

Let a valid \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) be given and abbreviate
\[
 p_N=c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N,
 \qquad
 q_D=d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D.
\]
By \texttt{def:gap-certificate}, \(y_N\) satisfies
\(B_{\mathrm{nested}}y_N=d_{\mathrm{nested}}\) and
\(y_N\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nested}}\).  Hence it is feasible for the
standard-form nested program in \texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}, and
therefore
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\le p_N. \tag{1}
\]
The exposing identities in \texttt{def:facial-dual} imply that every feasible
deep vector lies in \(F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\).  The certificate also gives
\[
 s_D:=c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
 \in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*.
\]
Consequently, for every deep feasible vector \(y\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}y-q_D
 &=\bigl(c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D\bigr)^{\top}y
   +\lambda_D^{\top}(B_{\mathrm{deep}}y-d_{\mathrm{deep}})\\
 &=s_D^{\top}y\ge0.
 \end{aligned} \tag{2}
\]
The last inequality is precisely the definition of the dual cone.  Taking the
infimum in (2), and using the equality between the standard-form objective and
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\), yields
\[
 q_D\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{3}
\]
No full-dimensional Slater condition or rank condition on
\(B_{\mathrm{deep}}\) is used in (2).

The certified interval inclusions and their strict separation give
\[
 p_N\le \sup I_N<\inf I_D\le q_D. \tag{4}
\]
Combining (1), (4), and (3) proves
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 \le p_N<q_D
 \le\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}},
\]
and hence \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\).  All equalities
and cone memberships preceding (4) are exact algebraic statements; outward
rational rounding is used only for the two objective enclosures.  Thus the
argument remains valid when weights vanish, constraints are redundant, or a
Lorentz block lies on a proper face.

In \(\mathsf I_*\), \(L=\delta=0\) and \(x_i=0\), so the predictor constraints
do not affect the objective.  By \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}, after minimizing
the epigraph variables, the objective is
\[
 \Gamma_s=z_B\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}
 \max_{h\in\{0,1\}}\|R_Qa_{1h}(w)\|_2. \tag{15}
\]
At time \(2\), every relevant diagonal entry of \(R_Q\) is one.  Under nested
support, write the early weights as \((w_2,w_3,w_4)\).  The treated coordinate
is distinct from every donor coordinate and has coefficient one, so
\[
 \|R_Qa_{1,0}(w)\|_2^2
 =1+w_2^2+w_3^2+w_4^2. \tag{16}
\]
The simplex restrictions give \(w_i\ge0\) and
\(w_2+w_3+w_4=1\).  Since
\[
 0\le (w_2-w_3)^2+(w_2-w_4)^2+(w_3-w_4)^2
 =3(w_2^2+w_3^2+w_4^2)-1,
\]
the sum of squares is at least \(1/3\), with equality if and only if
\(w_2=w_3=w_4=1/3\).  Thus the optimized early nested variance is \(4/3\).

The deep early support is \(\{3,4\}\).  For
\(w_3,w_4\ge0\) and \(w_3+w_4=1\),
\[
 \|R_Qa_{1,0}(w)\|_2^2=1+w_3^2+w_4^2
 \ge1+\frac12=\frac32, \tag{17}
\]
because \((w_3-w_4)^2\ge0\); equality holds exactly at
\((w_3,w_4)=(1/2,1/2)\).

At time \(3\), both rules use donors \(\{3,4\}\), and every relevant diagonal
entry of \(R_Q\) is \(1/10\).  Therefore
\[
 \|R_Qa_{1,1}(w)\|_2^2
 =\frac1{100}(1+w_3^2+w_4^2)
 \ge\frac1{100}\left(1+\frac12\right)=\frac3{200}, \tag{18}
\]
again with equality at equal weights.  The positive early standard deviations
\(\sqrt{4/3}\) and \(\sqrt{3/2}\) both exceed
\(\sqrt{3/200}\).  Because the feasible set is a product across horizons,
the separate equal-weight choices attain the minimum of the maximum in (15).
Using \(z_B=9/4\) gives
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 =\frac94\sqrt{\frac43}
 =\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}
 =\frac9{2\sqrt3},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}
 =\frac94\sqrt{\frac32}
 =\frac{9\sqrt6}{8}. \tag{19}
\]

The numerical enclosures follow by exact rational squaring of positive
endpoints:
\[
 2.5980^2=6.749604<\frac{27}{4}<6.75012361=2.5981^2
\]
and
\[
 2.7556^2=7.59333136<\frac{243}{32}<7.59388249=2.7557^2.
\]
Thus
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\in[2.5980,2.5981],
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\in[2.7556,2.7557].
\]
Subtracting outward endpoints yields
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 \in[2.7556-2.5981,\,2.7557-2.5980]
 =[0.1575,0.1577]. \tag{20}
\]
Finally, \(T_2=3\) implies \(2\in D_{1,0}\) because \(3>2\), while
\(2\notin D_{1,1}=D_{1K}\) because \(3\not>3\).  Hence the nested early rule
uses unit \(2\)'s still-untreated time-\(2\) outcome, whereas the common deep
pool excludes unit \(2\) at the early horizon solely because it adopts at the
late horizon.  All supports are nonempty, every displayed variance is
strictly positive, and no limiting argument is used.

theorem.statement:
For every finite rational input \(\mathsf{Data}\),
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{a valid finite }\mathsf{GapCert}\text{ exists}.
\]
There is an exact terminating construction and verifier using real-closed-field
quantifier elimination, exact polynomial reduction, and exact sign
determination on \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\); outward-rounded rational
arithmetic is used only for the two objective enclosures.  If \(d\) is the
total number of real variables in the two standard-form programs,
\(B\) is the binary input length, and
\(\Delta=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}>0\), put
\[
 \log_2^+(1/\Delta)=\max\{0,\log_2(1/\Delta)\}.
\]
For a universal constant \(\kappa_{\mathrm{alg}}>0\), the construction and
interval separation use
at most
\[
 \bigl(B+\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\rceil+1\bigr)^{2^{\kappa_{\mathrm{alg}}d}}
\]
bit operations.  The equivalence and algorithm require neither unique
optimizers, positive donor weights, independent predictor columns, ordinary
Slater feasibility, nor strict complementarity, and they cover tight and
collapsed Lorentz-cone blocks.  The positive part in the displayed complexity
bound is necessary because the model imposes no normalization forcing
\(\Delta\le1\).
theorem.proof_tex:
Write \(P_s\) for the standard-form program in
\texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}.  We first record two elementary facts
specific to these programs.

First, feasibility is common to the two support rules.  If the nested program
is feasible, then for every treated unit \(j\) its horizon-\(K\) simplex
\(\Delta(D_{jK})\) is nonempty.  Selecting any element of \(D_{jK}\) at every
horizon gives a feasible deep weight array, since the deep rule uses that same
set at all horizons.  Conversely, \(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\) for
\(h\le K\), because
\(T_i>T_j+K\) implies \(T_i>T_j+h\); hence deep feasibility implies nested
feasibility.  Thus the two programs are either both infeasible or both
feasible.  In particular, a strict inequality between their extended values
forces both to be feasible.

Second, whenever they are feasible, both values are finite and attained.  For
a fixed support rule, eliminate \(u\), \(v\), and \(g\) from
\texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}.  The resulting objective on the weight array is
\[
 G_s(w)=\max_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{
 L\left\|x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right\|_2
 +\delta+z_B\|R_Qa_{jh}(w)\|_2
 \right\}. \tag{5}
\]
Each nonempty donor simplex is closed and bounded, so their finite product
\(\mathcal F_s\) is compact.  Every affine map inside (5), the Euclidean norm,
and a finite maximum are continuous.  A minimizing sequence therefore has a
convergent subsequence in \(\mathcal F_s\), and continuity shows that its limit
attains the infimum.  Restoring the norm epigraph variables and nonnegative
slacks gives an attained optimum of \(P_s\).  Notice that this argument permits
zero weights and uses no predictor-rank condition.

We now prove the forward implication.  Assume
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}},
 \qquad
 \Delta:=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}>0. \tag{6}
\]
By the two facts above, choose a nested primal optimizer \(y_N^*\).  Apply
\texttt{lem:facial-reduction-relative-strong-duality} to the affine space
\(H_D=\{y:B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}}\}\) and the product cone
\(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}\).  It supplies an exposing chain
\[
 \mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}=F_0\supsetneq F_1\supsetneq\cdots
 \supsetneq F_r=F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}, \tag{7}
\]
exposing multipliers satisfying the identities in
\texttt{def:facial-dual}, and a point
\(y^\circ\in H_D\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}\).  The deep
objective is finite by (5); relative-interior strong duality therefore gives
an attained facial dual optimizer \(\lambda_D^*\) with
\[
 c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*
 \in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*,
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*
 =\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{8}
\]

All objects in (7)--(8) may be chosen real algebraic.  Here is the exact
reason.  Orthant membership is a list of linear weak inequalities, zero-cone
membership is a list of polynomial equalities, and
\[
 (t,z)\in\mathcal L_q
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 t\ge0\ \text{ and }\ t^2-\sum_{\nu=1}^{q-1}z_\nu^2\ge0. \tag{9}
\]
The faces of an orthant are coordinate faces.  The proper nonzero faces of a
Lorentz cone are rays, in addition to the zero face: a proper face cannot
contain an interior point, while the midpoint of two noncollinear nonzero
boundary vectors is interior by the strict triangle inequality.  A face of a
product cone is a product of faces, because decomposing a point as the sum of
its block-supported components and applying the face property puts each
component in the face.  Thus every relevant face, its relative interior, and
its dual are described by finitely many polynomial equalities and strict or
weak sign conditions with algebraic coefficients.  The finitely many face
types and chain lengths \(r\le d\) can be enumerated.  Equivalently, one can
retain the recursive orthogonal-exposure description in (7).  The requirements
\[
 z_k\in F_{k-1}^*,\quad
 z_k=B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k,\quad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k=0,\quad
 F_k=F_{k-1}\cap z_k^\perp, \tag{10}
\]
together with strict face reduction, relative-interior feasibility, nested
primal optimality, and facial-dual optimality form a first-order formula over
the rationals.  Primal and dual optimality can be written with one universal
competitor block following one existential certificate block.  This formula
has a real solution by (7)--(8) and attainment.  Effective real-algebraic
elimination and sampling from
\texttt{lem:effective-real-algebraic-elimination} therefore give a solution
all of whose coordinates lie in \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\).  Denote the
sampled optimizers again by \(y_N^*\) and \(\lambda_D^*\).  Their objective
values
\[
 p_N:=c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N^*=\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}},
 \qquad
 q_D:=d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}} \tag{11}
\]
are real algebraic and satisfy \(q_D-p_N=\Delta\).

Exact real-root isolation gives nested outward rational intervals around
\(p_N\) and \(q_D\).  The algorithm refines both and stops at the first exact
rational test \(\sup I_N<\inf I_D\).  This test must eventually succeed:
once both widths are less than \(\Delta/3\),
\[
 \sup I_N
 <p_N+\Delta/3
 <q_D-\Delta/3
 <\inf I_D, \tag{12}
\]
after harmless further refinement if an endpoint equality occurs.  The face
chain, the algebraic points, and the intervals at that stopping time are
exactly the fields of \(\mathsf{GapCert}\), so (6) implies existence of a valid
finite certificate.  The stopping rule itself does not require \(\Delta\) as
an additional input; \(\Delta\) only bounds the number of refinements.

Conversely, if a valid \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) exists, then
\texttt{prop:strict-gap-sufficient} gives
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\).  This proves the
equivalence.

We next justify termination and the advertised complexity.  A chain has length
at most the dimension of the deep cone, hence at most \(d\).  Before
quantifier elimination, exact rational row reduction is applied to the linear
map
\[
 \eta\longmapsto
 \bigl(B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta,\,
       d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta\bigr).
\]
Its range has dimension at most the number of deep primal coordinates plus
one, so each exposing multiplier can be represented during elimination by at
most \(d+1\) active coordinates; a full multiplier is recovered afterward by
setting the unused coordinates to zero in the selected column basis.  This
row reduction is valid even when the equality rows are redundant.  Storing the
elimination variables for all chain vectors, compressed exposing multipliers,
primal points, and dual points therefore uses \(O(d^2)\) real variables.  The
possibly longer displayed full multipliers have total size polynomial in
\(B\) times this bound.  The certificate-existence and optimality formula
has a fixed number of quantifier blocks, polynomially many rational atoms,
degree at most two before standard auxiliary-variable reductions, and binary
length polynomial in \(B\).  The fixed-block bound in
\texttt{lem:effective-real-algebraic-elimination} is therefore bounded by
\[
 (B+1)^{2^{C_0d}} \tag{13}
\]
for a universal constant \(C_0\); this deliberately loose envelope absorbs
every polynomial in \(d\), as well as algebraic sample construction and exact
sign determination.  Refining algebraic isolating intervals until (12) adds a
number of bit operations polynomial in the representation size and in
\(\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\rceil+1\).  Increasing the universal constant gives
\[
 \bigl(B+\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\rceil+1\bigr)^{2^{Cd}}. \tag{14}
\]
The verifier reduces every affine equality in (10) and every primal or dual
equality to an exact polynomial identity in the algebraic representations, and
uses exact sign determination for (9), orthant signs, strict face reductions,
and relative-interior signs.  It uses outward rational arithmetic only to
check the two objective enclosures and the strict rational comparison in
(12).

No part of this construction chooses an inverse, a basis of predictor columns,
a unique optimizer, or a strictly complementary solution.  A zero donor
weight is an allowed boundary point of an orthant; redundant predictors merely
repeat polynomial constraints; and tight or collapsed Lorentz blocks are
carried into the appropriate proper face in (7).  Hence all degeneracies named
in the statement are included.

Finally, without the positive part in (14), the requested expression can
decrease when \(\Delta>1\), although reading the input alone costs order
\(B\) bit operations.  Since the frozen model has no scale normalization that
forces \(\Delta\le1\), replacing \(\log_2(1/\Delta)\) by
\(\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\) is necessary and is the exact separation-sensitive
bound proved here.  This is a finite exact result; no asymptotic limit is
taken.

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(\mathcal K_0\) be a finite-dimensional closed convex cone and let
\(\mathcal H_0\) be an affine space with
\(\mathcal H_0\cap\mathcal K_0\ne\varnothing\).  There is a finite strict facial
reduction sequence whose successive orthogonal exposures reach the minimal
face \(\mathcal F_0\) of \(\mathcal K_0\) containing
\(\mathcal H_0\cap\mathcal K_0\), and
\(\mathcal H_0\cap\operatorname{ri}\mathcal F_0\ne\varnothing\).  Replacing
\(\mathcal K_0\) by \(\mathcal F_0\) preserves
the feasible set; for a conic linear objective with finite primal value, the
dual over \(\mathcal F_0^*\) has the same value and attains it.

added_lemmas.statement:
For a first-order formula over a real closed field whose atoms are polynomial
sign conditions with integer coefficients, effective quantifier elimination
terminates, produces an equivalent quantifier-free formula, and can produce
real-algebraic sample points for every nonempty sign condition.  With a fixed
number of quantifier blocks, the bit complexity and the degrees and coefficient
heights of the resulting algebraic representations are bounded by the input
bit length raised to an exponent polynomial in the block dimensions; exact
arithmetic and sign determination at the represented real-algebraic points are
effective within the same singly-exponential-in-dimension envelope.

proofs.proof_tex:
Assume that \(D_{jh}=D_{jK}\) for every \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  Fix \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  Equality of the supporting index sets gives equality of the corresponding simplexes,
\[
\Delta(D_{jh})=\Delta(D_{jK}).
\]
Taking the finite Cartesian product over \(e\in\mathcal E\) and using the construction of \(\mathcal F_s\) therefore yields
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jh})
=\prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jK})
=\mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{1}
\]

For clarity, let \(\mathcal B_s\) be the set of pairs \((w,\ell)\) that satisfy all constraints in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} for support rule \(s\).  In that definition the support-rule label occurs only through the requirement \(w\in\mathcal F_s\): the model class, estimator \(\widehat\tau(w)\), target \(\tau\), deterministic-width restriction, and uniform coverage event are otherwise the same for the two rules.  Consequently, (1) implies
\[
\mathcal B_{\mathrm{nested}}=\mathcal B_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{2}
\]
The objective is the same map \((w,\ell)\mapsto\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e\) on both sets.  Applying the construction in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} to (2) gives, equation by equation,
\[
W_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{nested}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
=\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal B_{\mathrm{deep}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
=W_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{3}
\]
This equality remains valid under the extended-value convention in the definition even if the common admissible set is empty.

Likewise, let \(\mathcal S_s\) denote the feasible set of tuples \((w,u,v,g)\) in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}.  The only support-rule-dependent constraint is \(w\in\mathcal F_s\).  All remaining constraints use the same fixed predictors, contrast-row map, covariance factor, constants, and coordinate set.  Hence (1) gives
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}=\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{4}
\]
Since both conic programs minimize the same scalar coordinate \(g\), (4) and \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} imply
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}}g
=\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}}g
=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\tag{5}
\]
Equations (3) and (5) prove both asserted equalities.  No covariance rank, positivity, Gaussian, overlap, boundary, or limiting condition is used: the result follows solely from equality of the finite support-restricted feasible sets.
